faqs.a: HSL separates hue (the color family), saturation (intensity), and lightness. It is much easier to build a palette - for example, keep the same hue and change lightness for shades and tints.
faqs.q: Why does it show HSL too?

faqs.a: Semi-transparent pixels report their blended RGB values, and RGBA shows the exact alpha from the file. So a 50 percent red over white reports as rgb(255, 128, 128) with rgba(255, 0, 0, 0.5).
faqs.q: What does it show for transparent pixels?

image-color-picker.formula:
HSL from RGB:
max = highest of R, G, B (0-1). min = lowest. delta = max - min.
hue = 60 x (G - B) / delta (when red is max)
lightness = (max + min) / 2
saturation = delta / (1 - |2 x lightness - 1|)
Example: RGB(255, 0, 0): max = 1, min = 0, delta = 1.
hue = 0 deg, lightness = 0.5, saturation = 1 -> hsl(0, 100%, 50%).
howTo: Choose an image file (JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP or SVG) up to 25 MB.
Move your cursor over the image - the preview box shows the color under it.
Click (or tap) any pixel to lock it in as your picked color.
Read the HEX, RGB, RGBA and HSL values and copy any of them with one click.
Change the image any time with the Change file link.
keyFacts: A pixel color is three numbers: red, green and blue, each from 0 to 255.
HEX is the same value written as six hex digits, for example #FF0000 for pure red.
RGBA adds a fourth channel: alpha, the transparency from 0 (invisible) to 1 (solid).
HSL expresses the same color as hue, saturation and lightness - easier for humans to adjust.
The picker reads the raw pixel data from the image, not what your screen shows.
On touch devices, tap a pixel directly to pick it.

limitations: It reads pixel data, not perceived color - screen brightness and color profiles can make the same HEX look different.
Heavily compressed JPEGs smear edges, so the pixel you click may be a blend of two colors.
Hover picking needs a mouse; touch users tap instead, which is less precise.
It cannot read colors from videos or from images on other websites directly.

image-color-picker.workedExample:
Click a pure-red pixel (RGB values 255, 0, 0).
1. HEX: each channel as two hex digits -> FF 00 00 -> #FF0000.
2. RGB: rgb(255, 0, 0).
3. RGBA: alpha 255 / 255 = 1 -> rgba(255, 0, 0, 1).
4. HSL: max = 1 (red), min = 0, delta = 1.
   hue = 60 x ((0 - 0) / 1) = 0 degrees.
   lightness = (1 + 0) / 2 = 0.5 -> 50%.
   saturation = 1 / (1 - |1 - 1|) = 1 -> 100%.
5. Result: hsl(0, 100%, 50%).
